edit.description: read_collection_member (222) takes a LayoutMember's leaves from its immediate sub-headings only, keyed by slug; the paragraph directly under the member's own heading lands nowhere. Land it under whichever reserved leaf key `(layout-own-span-leaf)` rules — composed leaves are author-named (NestedMemberRow.leaves keyed by field name, no reserved own-span key exists there; the SDK's `FRAMEWORK_KEYS`/kind.ts:245 `prose` is a member-level value, not a leaf-name reservation). Hazards the fork must rule on: node.body includes sub-heading text (the own span must cut at the first child heading), and a sub-heading slugged to the reserved name would collide with it.
Regression: a layout collection member whose body is `### Title` + a paragraph + `**Test.** ...` (no sub-headings) materializes a non-empty leaves map carrying the paragraph under the ruled key.

FRAMEWORK_KEYS (~245) reserves `prose` as a member-level value only; once `(layout-own-span-leaf)` rules a reserved own-span leaf key, an author's sub-heading slugging to that same name needs a collision guard (or explicit precedence rule) — the exact key and whether it joins FRAMEWORK_KEYS stays whatever the fork rules, not invented here.

summary: A layout collection member's own paragraph span lands nowhere — not a leaf, not the lock, not explain — while its sub-headings' spans do.

edit.description: `narrate_kind` (:534, binding the `KindFactRow` at :544 and holding the whole `kind_facts` slice at :537) renders three strands — guidance and cite, layout regions plus skeleton, hosted kinds — and nothing else (:534-582), so a kind whose row declares only guidance prints one line and stops. Three more strands, all renderable off data already in hand, no signature change: (i) the **locus** — and it is NOT either/or: `hook` carries `governs_root = ".claude"`, `governs_glob = "settings.json"` AND `collection_address = { manifest, key_path }`, so render the collection address (in src/drift.rs: the `KindFactRow` column at :3440, its `manifest`/`key_path` fields at :3479/:3482) as where the MEMBER keys and `governs_root`/`governs_glob` (:3390/:3394) as where the host document is discovered, plus the `registration` channel labels (:3417 — the wire spelling is the call form the SDK writes, `event(event)` for `hook`, per sdk/src/declarations.ts:219-234 and .temper/lock.toml:72) and the `commitment` class (:3405), which is part of where a member lands (a local kind's members are uncommitted); a file-locus kind shows the governs line alone. (ii) the **hosting kinds** inverse — which kinds host members of this one — restored, not dropped: it is the prerequisite for (iii), because the row cannot say whether a member is top-level or embedded (`orientation` is embedded yet its row carries `unit_shape = "file"` and no `governs`), and the oracle is a scan over the other `kind_facts` rows' path-less `templates` entries and `content.regions[].member_kind` for this kind's name. (iii) the **address form** — `<kind>:<name>` for a top-level kind, `<host-address>/<kind>/<key>` for one only ever hosted, EMBEDDED VALUE OR FILE CHILD ALIKE: a nested-file child is a `[[declaration.nested_member]]` row carrying `host = "skill:test-skill"` (tests/coverage_note.rs:391-396), so `supporting-doc` takes the host-qualified form exactly as an embedded value does. Which means strand (ii)'s oracle must scan path-BEARING `templates` entries too, not only path-less ones, or a file-child kind's hosts go unnamed and (iii) has nothing to read — read from the single address-grammar home MEMBER-ADDRESS-GRAMMAR-ONE-HOME establishes (`src/member_address.rs`), never a second hand-spelling. Two mechanics: the early return at :554-567 ("nothing to teach") fires when guidance, cite, layout, embedded and file-children are all absent, so it must gain the locus and hosting terms or the new strands never print; and the address form must ride that same guard rather than rendering unconditionally off the kind name, or `explain_narrates_a_kind_absent_guidance_cleanly` (tests/read_verbs.rs:1065, which passes `&[]` rows) goes red. Reword that line from "nothing to teach before a member of it exists" to naming the strands. All of this must render with ZERO members of the kind in the corpus — the adopter's actual moment, and the reason this is not `corpus_leaves` (:817), which can only report what existing members carry.

Regressions on a MEMBER-LESS surface, per tests[] — the non-vacuity bar is that the fixture carries zero members of the explained kind, so the lines cannot be coming from a corpus read. `explain_kind` (:819) is the helper both new tests use; it synthesizes contracts from the rows, so a kind is only resolvable if it has a row. Keep the existing arm at :1065 where a kind with no row at all still prints its clean "nothing declared" line rather than falling silent. It is NOT byte-for-byte: it asserts `contains("No authoring guidance is declared")` (:1101) and the absence of a `‣` marker (:1105), so the reword must keep that opening clause and may change only the tail after the em dash — and the address form must ride the same guard, or the arm goes red on the marker-free line growing an address it has no row to source. No snapshot moves: nothing under tests/snapshots/ asserts explain-kind output, and every CLI-driven `common::explain_in` call in the tree targets a MEMBER, never a kind — tests/layout_kind.rs, tests/lock_declaration_rows.rs, tests/layout_edge_slot.rs:259 (`guide`) and tests/requirement_roster.rs:742/:846 (`data-retention`, `memory-doc`) — so `narrate_kind`'s new strands reach none of them (ripple-reconciled at bb246cc2).

VERIFY-ONLY — expect no diff. The `kind_facts(name, governs_root, governs_glob)` builder (:614-631) always sets BOTH governs fields, so every existing bare-kind test that builds a row gains a locus line: tests/read_verbs.rs:763, :915, :970, :1015. All four assert with `contains`, so they stay green while their output grows. In the fence so the builder can gain a no-locus variant if a new arm needs one, not because an edit is expected.

edit.description: `defersToGate` (:77-80) is the one reader of the host-address grammar still spelling it by hand — `address.includes("/")`, then `indexOf(":")` with a `colon > 0` test — beside `sdk/src/member-address.ts`, which f35c06e6 (SDK-MEMBER-ADDRESS-GRAMMAR-ONE-HOME) made the home the twenty-one writers round-trip against. Route it through `parseHostAddress`: `const host = parseHostAddress(address); return host !== undefined && deferrableKinds.has(host.kind);`. The doc comment above it restates the `/` and `:` rules in prose — rewrite it to cite the grammar module's reader rather than re-spell the segments, and name the verdict it now takes on a name-less address.

`parseHostAddress` (:100) refuses an empty kind and an empty name; narrow it so a name carrying `/` is no host address either — the `/` is this grammar's own segment separator (`segment`, :120, splits on it) and the segmented spellings have their own readers (`parseNestedAddress`, `parseLeafAddress`). That is what lets `defersToGate` drop its `includes("/")` guard without changing its verdict on a nested or leaf address: an unresolved `skill:x/hook/on-enter` must keep refusing at emit, not defer because `skill` is deferrable. The narrowing lands here rather than as a second guard at the call site because the function's only callers today are this module and its test (`rg parseHostAddress sdk/src`).

`declaredAtLocusKinds`'s doc (:975-979) states the deferral signal in prose and points at `prose.ts`'s `defersToGate`; ride the new name-less verdict into that sentence if it no longer reads true. Verify-only otherwise — no code change is expected here.

The round-trip arm (:24-38) pins `["collaboration", ":collaboration", "rule:"]` as the segment-shaped holes `parseHostAddress` answers `undefined` for; add a `/`-carrying name (e.g. `skill:x/hook/on-enter`) to that list, so the narrowing is pinned where the grammar's own reader is tested.

The two verdicts this consolidation moves, pinned beside the existing deferral arms (:95 defers on a declared at-locus kind, :113 refuses on an undeclared one): a mention of `<declared-at-locus-kind>:` — no name — refuses at emit (`a mention cannot dangle`) where it defers today, and an unresolved nested-shaped address whose head kind IS deferrable still refuses, the verdict `includes("/")` holds today and `parseHostAddress` holds after.

summary: `defersToGate` hand-reads the host-address grammar beside the module that owns it — route it through the grammar's reader and pin the two verdicts that moves.
